chunks: And 'Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' at the time of your sleep, for they are a discharge from polytheism, and 'Qul Huwa Allahu' is the attribute of the Lord."

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Recite: He is Allah, the One) - Surah Al-Ikhlas
key_terms.قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ: Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun (Recite: O you disbelievers) - Surah Al-Kafirun

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Al-Kafirun before sleeping?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the spiritual practice of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun before sleep as a means of safeguarding against polytheism (shirk). The text specifically characterizes Surah Al-Ikhlas as defining the attribute of Lordship (Nisbat al-Rabb), while Surah Al-Kafirun serves as a declaration of disassociation from idolatry, reflecting the Shia emphasis on Tawhid in daily devotional routines.
